description: internal/users: the account listing. Every mutant here is a way a child stops appearing on the dashboard; the package's whole stance is that a missed account is the dangerous direction, so the guards that keep and report are tested as hard as the ones that drop.

mutants.note: the UID_MAX ceiling stops filtering, so an account parked above it -- a container or LDAP uid -- is offered as a local child
no uid filter at all: root and every system account appear as people to lock out
service accounts that cannot hold a session are listed as lockable, burying the real accounts in dozens of rows
no-login shells matched by substring, which also drops a real shell whose name happens to contain the word -- the direction that hides a child
the declared-no-home exclusion is gone, so accounts useradd wrote with no home are offered as people

a home that is merely absent right now -- an unmounted volume, an NFS home that has not mounted -- drops the account. This is the fail-open direction the package exists to avoid, and it drops it in silence
the missing-home note is never written, so an account kept on a guess is presented as a certainty
a truncated record is parsed instead of skipped, so a password file cut off mid-write loses its tail without a word
the field-count test inverted: well-formed records are skipped and malformed ones parsed
an empty login name is listed; it cannot be shown or acted on, and it is not the filter working
a duplicate username is appended without a note, so which home and uid won is invisible
comments in login.defs are parsed as keys; harmless for the two keys read here, but it is the branch that keeps a commented file out of the notes
keys matched case-sensitively, so a file that spells uid_min lower-case silently gets the default floor
the assumed UID_MIN is never announced. The assumption is not neutral -- 1000 hides the first human on an old Red Hat system -- so making it silently is the failure
the assumed UID_MAX is never announced
an inverted range is reported as an empty machine rather than as a file that contradicts itself
a login.defs that fails mid-read yields the defaults as if the file had been read cleanly
a password file that fails mid-read yields whatever was parsed before the fault, so a truncated file reads as a short machine
"nothing looked human" is returned as success. An empty list is a fact about the machine; this is a fact about the configuration, and the caller cannot tell them apart
the zero Source stops pointing at the password file, so an unconfigured web layer reads a file that cannot answer and reports an empty machine
the default home check stops checking, so the declared-no-home rule is the only one left and every phantom home is presented as a real one
every row claims to be live, so an account that left the machine keeps reporting itself as protected
a configured-and-enabled row for an account that no longer exists counts as coverage. The code says the parent did everything right; the row protects nobody
an account configured but switched off counts as managed, so the dashboard reports full coverage on a machine where nothing is enabled
rows come back in map order. The screen paginates, so a row that moves between loads is worse than a slow load
the row aliases the caller's slice. internal/config is copy-on-write, so an edit leaves this row reading a document nothing still calls current
the config half aliases the caller's slice, so a page can disagree with the file it claims to show
